_readme: SAIRNlaw deadline engine seed -- STATE requests for production of documents.
Phase 7. Ohio, Indiana, Michigan and Pennsylvania.
Every value read from primary source 2026-08-23 and quoted in the row.
These are the four rules disclosed as unread in Phases 5 and 6, where the
standing note was that their absence meant NOT YET VERIFIED rather than
verified absent. They are now read.
THE FINDING: THE DESIGNATED-PERIOD SHAPE IS A PROPERTY OF THE STATE'S
DISCOVERY REGIME, NOT OF THE PARTICULAR DEVICE. Each of the four states was
checked on this rule directly rather than assumed to follow its own
interrogatory and admission rules -- and the split turned out perfectly
consistent by state across all three discovery devices:
interrogatories   admissions     production
Ohio               designated (28)   designated(28) DESIGNATED (28)
Indiana            designated (30)   designated(30) DESIGNATED (30)
Michigan           fixed 28          fixed 28       FIXED 28
Pennsylvania       fixed 30          fixed 30       FIXED 30
(US Federal        fixed 30          fixed 30       fixed 30)
That consistency is not an assumption this file made -- it is the result of
reading twelve rules across three phases. It is worth recording precisely
because it now makes a PREDICTION about any further Ohio or Indiana
discovery device: expect a designated period, and verify it anyway.
Ohio Civ.R. 34(B)  'within a period designated in the request that is not
less than twenty-eight days after the service of the
request or within a shorter or longer time as the
court may allow'
Ind. T.R. 34(B)    'The party upon whom the request is served must serve a
written response within a period designated in the
request, not less than thirty days after service'
Both use the designated_period shape built in Phase 6 -- the requesting
party's chosen figure is a required input, the rule's number is only the
floor, and a below-floor designation is REFUSED rather than raised. NO new
engine capability was needed or added for this phase; the existing shape
covers these rules exactly, which is the outcome that should follow from
having built it against the rule text rather than against two rules.
MICHIGAN AND PENNSYLVANIA ARE FIXED, verified rather than inferred from
their own sibling rules:
Mich. Ct. R. 2.310(C)(2)  'must serve a written response within 28 days
after service of the request, except that a
defendant may serve a response within 42 days
after being served with the summons and
complaint'
Pa.R.C.P. 4009.12         'within thirty days after the service of the
request'
Michigan carries the same defendant-specific alternative its interrogatory
and admission rules do -- 42 days running from service of PROCESS, a
genuinely different trigger event, so it is its own rule with its own
trigger name. Four Michigan rules now run from service of process in this
jurisdiction (answer, interrogatories, admissions, production) and each
needs a distinct trigger name or the engine refuses AMBIGUOUS_RULE rather
than choosing between them.
Pennsylvania has NO defendant provision here, unlike its own Rule 4014(b)
which carries a 45-day defendant floor for admissions. Same chapter,
different shape -- another reason each rule was read rather than inferred.
NO SERVICE EXTENSION on any rule here. Michigan sets a different PERIOD
rather than adding days; Pennsylvania has no automatic mail extension at
all (Phase 3 finding 6); and the validator structurally blocks one on a
designated-period rule, since the designated figure already is the period.
WHAT REMAINS UNREAD, disclosed on the same standard: Ohio Civ.R. 36's and
Indiana T.R. 36's subpoena-to-non-party analogues, and every state's
deposition-notice timing. Absence means not yet verified, not verified
absent.

rules.label: Response to a request for production — period designated in the request (Ohio)

authority.quote: within a period designated in the request that is not less than twenty-eight days after the service of the request or within a shorter or longer time as the court may allow
authority.note: THIS RULE SETS NO DEADLINE. Twenty-eight days is the minimum a valid request may demand; the deadline is whatever the serving party designated. Same shape as Ohio Civ.R. 33(A) and 36(A)(1), verified on this rule's own text rather than carried over from them. The court may also allow a shorter or longer time, quoted above — the engine has no field for a court order, so a computed date here is the request's designated period, not a court-modified one.

rules.label: Response to a request for production — period designated in the request (Indiana)

authority.quote: The party upon whom the request is served must serve a written response within a period designated in the request, not less than thirty days after service
authority.note: Indiana's floor is THIRTY where Ohio's is twenty-eight, the same two-day divergence their interrogatory and admission rules carry. The two rules are near-identically worded and differ in the number, which is exactly why each state is read separately rather than one inferred from the other. Computed under indiana_tr_6a, whose sub-seven-day exclusion is gated on the figure actually counted (the designated period), not on the floor.

rules.label: Response to a request for production of documents (Michigan)

authority.quote: The party on whom the request is served must serve a written response within 28 days after service of the request, except that a defendant may serve a response within 42 days after being served with the summons and complaint.
authority.note: A FIXED period, verified on this rule's own text and not inferred from MCR 2.309/2.312 sharing the figure. Unlike Ohio Civ.R. 34(B) and Ind. T.R. 34(B), which set only a floor on a party-designated period, Michigan states the deadline itself. The 42-day defendant alternative runs from service of PROCESS, a different trigger event, and is its own rule here. No service_extension: Michigan handles manner of service by setting a different period rather than adding days.

rules.label: Response to a request for production by a defendant, counted from service of process (Michigan)

authority.quote: except that a defendant may serve a response within 42 days after being served with the summons and complaint
authority.note: The FOURTH Michigan rule running from service of process in this jurisdiction — after the answer, the interrogatory defendant period and the admission defendant period. Each carries a distinct trigger name because four rules sharing one trigger would be refused as AMBIGUOUS_RULE rather than chosen between. As with the sibling rules, the defendant MAY use this period, so early in a case both this and the 28-day period from the request can be running.

rules.label: Response to a request for production of documents and things (Pennsylvania)

authority.quote: within thirty days after the service of the request
authority.note: A fixed thirty days with NO defendant provision — unlike Pennsylvania's own Rule 4014(b), which carries a 45-day defendant floor for admissions. Same chapter of the same rule set, different shape, which is why this was read rather than inferred from its sibling. No service_extension: Pennsylvania has no automatic mail extension at all. effective_from is 2024-01-01 for the same reason as every other Pennsylvania rule here — that is when Pa.R.J.A. 107 took effect and Pa.R.C.P. 106 was rescinded, and this row is the pairing of the count with a computation standard.
